_doc: Farmland is painted crop by crop: each field grows one crop, and only that crop's building goes up on it (land painted before crops existed takes any). 'building' is the farm that grows it; its goods and their amounts are that building's in buildings.json. 'seasons' replaces the season's yield for the good (seasons.json) for that crop's farms, so a crop keeps its own calendar; a crop without it follows the season's yields. Crops unlock with their building's charter. The order is saved by number: only ever add crops at the end. 'share' is the part of the town's farms the stand-in mayor sows with it; it also sows a field of whatever farm the town wants most when none is open for it.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.blurb: Bread for every table. A big harvest in late summer and autumn, almost nothing in winter.

crops.name: Root crops
crops.blurb: Less food than wheat, but steady all year: what the town eats when the snow lies on the fields.

crops.name: Barley & hops
crops.blurb: Brewed on the farm into ale for the taverns, with some grain to spare.

crops.name: Orchard
crops.blurb: Apples, pears and cider. Bare most of the year, then a great crop at harvest.

crops.name: Pasture
crops.blurb: Sheep for wool and mutton. Shearing in spring.

crops.name: Herb beds
crops.blurb: Healing herbs for the apothecaries, best in summer.

crops.name: Vineyard
crops.blurb: Wine for the manors and high tables. The vintage comes in autumn.
